question.worked_solution:
Recall the following:

- a function $f(x)$ is *even* if $f(-x)=f(x),$

- a function $f(x)$ is *odd* if $f(-x)=-f(x).$

Moreover, for any odd function $f(x),$ the graph of $y=f(x)$ has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin. Therefore, we have

$$
{\int }_{-a}^{a}f(x)\,\text{d}x=0.
$$

Notice that $f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{7})$ is an odd function. Indeed, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-x) & =sin\,((-x)^{7}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(-{x}^{7}) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{7}) \\  & =-f(x).\end{aligned}
$$

So, because $f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{7})$ is an odd function, we have

$$
{\int }_{-\sqrt{\pi }}^{\sqrt{\pi }}\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{7})\,\text{d}x=0.
$$
